items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: I remember Turk Murphy, I sat in with Turk’s band out in San Francisco.

ctx.x: I was going to ask you about that. Because the list people that you’ve played with, if you go from Dizzy Gillespie to Al Hirt, do you try to tailor your playing to better match with what those people are doing?

I think you do. I really think you do. And thank God I had enough technical ability to be able to do that. And I guess that’s not really bragging I mean it’s just — you know I remember Turk Murphy, I sat in with Turk’s band out in San Francisco. I loved that band. I just — there was a romance about that whole San Francisco thing that I really liked it. And I was playing and got done, and we’re down in Turk’s break room where everybody’s filling up their pipes with all this magic stuff. And I never really got into…

Our benefactor, who started this project, was a frequent attender at these jazz parties. And I recall he would say something like, he’s look at the list of musicians and go, “Oh yeah I like him, oh Watrous well too many notes.” He would say that kind of thing. And I know that certain players would sort of temper their approach when they looked out at the audience and assess what they see.
